A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MENTAT study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and matchable; v1's appendices are retained alongside two new explanatory appendices in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original clinician-annotation analyses and language-model experiments measuring task accuracy, demographic sensitivity, and free-form response inconsistency.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports a brief qualitative analysis of triage and documentation failures.

M1.justification: The annotation pipeline, hierarchical Bradley-Terry model, regularized objective, parameter bounds, softmax labels, and invalid-answer postprocessing are unchanged. New Appendix D explains the existing model choice without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 203-question dataset, five clinical task categories, demographic variations, and free-form evaluation coverage. V2's Appendix B illustrates existing questions rather than reporting added datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: The model sets in Figure 4 and Table 3 and the Bradley-Terry comparison in Figure 3 are unchanged. MMedS-Llama-3-8B receives additional discussion but was already evaluated; Meditron-7b scores are omitted in both versions.

E3.justification: The 183/20 question split, generated evaluation-set sizes, model versions, prompts, temperatures, and scoring procedures remain unchanged. V2's explicit 18–65 demographic-variable range clarifies the age coverage already reflected in v1's evaluation.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 newly reports a qualitative investigation of failure patterns in triage and documentation. This is a limited additional error analysis; the annotation comparisons, demographic analyses, and prompt checks are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain bootstrap uncertainty estimates, 95% confidence reporting, ten free-form responses per question, and the same annotation-disagreement analyses. V2 introduces no new repeated-run information or statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the matched result plots retain their numerical values. Section 4.2 adds qualitative findings, including unreliable extraction of relevant clinical information in documentation responses without a single identified failure pattern.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), model assumptions, and mathematical processing remain unchanged. Appendix D supplies background and intuitive motivation, without adding a formal definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and central conclusion retain MENTAT's clinician-created, five-domain evaluation contribution and its ambiguity, demographic-sensitivity, and free-form evaluation use cases. The additional discussion elaborates these contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving safety-training conflicts and information extraction, interprets the retained MMedS results as caution about synthetic training, and explicitly limits MENTAT to assessing equal-to-human performance. These extend the existing discussion of bias and applicability limits.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly documents the demographic age-variable range and describes the GitHub dataset as encrypted. Appendix B also explains withholding sample answer options to reduce contamination. These are new disclosures; the PDFs do not establish when encryption was introduced.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands methodological positioning through Appendix D's connections to Bradley-Terry modeling, preference-based reinforcement learning, and language-model alignment. It also adds comparisons with AIME, HumanEval, and BIG-Bench Hard and broader uncertainty, evaluation-validity, and mental-health-safety literature.

P1.justification: V2 adds explanatory appendices for sample questions and Bradley-Terry motivation, expands selected design and discussion paragraphs, and updates cross-references and acknowledgements. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Appendix B adds boxed Figures 6–14 showing question stems across four task categories. Existing plots, tables, prompt displays, and the interface screenshot retain their designs and content, with relocation and renumbering accompanying the additions.

improvement.justification: The sample questions, annotation-model rationale, and clearer scope and access disclosures make the dataset easier to understand and assess than in v1. Quantitative evidence remains unchanged. The added failure explanations lack detailed supporting analysis, limiting their evidential value, but the overall gains in clarity and transparency support a modest improvement.
